We’ve first conducted a data analysis focusing on the relationship between Group A: Visa and Mastercard; Group B: Coca-Cola and Pepsi.

# 2. Data Description

Monthly adjusted closing price data for Visa (V) and Mastercard (MA) ; Coca_Cola (KO) and Pepsi (PEP) was collected from Yahoo Finance for the period between January 2019 and January 2024. Adjusted closing prices were chosen because they account for dividends and stock splits, providing accurate reflections of true market performance.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(quantmod)
library(xts)
library(dplyr)
library(zoo)
library(PerformanceAnalytics)
library(urca)
install.packages("egcm")
install.packages("KFAS")

start_date <- as.Date("2019-01-01")
end_date   <- as.Date("2024-01-01")

# Group A:
getSymbols("V", src = "yahoo", from = start_date, to = end_date, periodicity = "monthly")
getSymbols("MA", src = "yahoo", from = start_date, to = end_date, periodicity = "monthly")

V_adj <- Ad(V)
MA_adj <- Ad(MA)

prices_V_MA <- merge(V_adj, MA_adj)
colnames(prices_V_MA) <- c("V", "MA")

# Group B:
getSymbols("KO", src = "yahoo", from = start_date, to = end_date, periodicity = "monthly")
getSymbols("PEP", src = "yahoo", from = start_date, to = end_date, periodicity = "monthly")

KO_adj <- Ad(KO)
PEP_adj <- Ad(PEP)

prices_KO_PEP <- merge(KO_adj, PEP_adj)
colnames(prices_KO_PEP) <- c("KO", "PEP")

# Group C:
getSymbols("GLD", src = "yahoo", from = start_date, to = end_date, periodicity = "monthly")
getSymbols("IAU", src = "yahoo", from = start_date, to = end_date, periodicity = "monthly")

GLD_adj <- Ad(GLD)
IAU_adj <- Ad(IAU)

prices_GLD_IAU <- merge(GLD_adj, IAU_adj)
colnames(prices_GLD_IAU) <- c("GLD", "IAU")


# Verification of Cointegrated Time Series Stability for Further Analysis (Group C)
library(egcm)

# Engle-Granger Cointegration Test for Group C (GLD & IAU)
egcm_test_GLD_IAU <- egcm(prices_GLD_IAU$GLD, prices_GLD_IAU$IAU)
summary(egcm_test_GLD_IAU)

# Residual stability check
residual_GLD_IAU <- prices_GLD_IAU$GLD - egcm_test_GLD_IAU$beta * prices_GLD_IAU$IAU - egcm_test_GLD_IAU$alpha
plot(residual_GLD_IAU, type="l", main="Engle-Granger Cointegration Residuals (GLD & IAU)", col="blue")
abline(h=mean(residual_GLD_IAU), col="red", lwd=2)
```

head(prices_V_MA)
summary(prices_V_MA)

plot(prices_V_MA, main = "Monthly Adjusted Closing Prices for V and MA", col = c("blue", "red"))
```

summary(prices_KO_PEP)

plot(prices_KO_PEP, main = "Monthly Adjusted Closing Prices for KO and PEP", col = c("blue", "red"))
```

# 3. Methodology

## 3.1 Cointegration Test

The Johansen cointegration test was performed to assess whether Visa and Mastercard share a statistically significant long-term equilibrium relationship.

```{r}
# Group A: 
GroupA_test <- ca.jo(prices_V_MA, type = "trace", ecdet = "const", K = 2)
summary(GroupA_test)
```

The test results indicate a statistically significant cointegration relationship, meaning these two assets tend to revert toward a long-run equilibrium. The identified cointegration relationship is:

\[
V - 0.5453 \times MA - 23.6470 = 0
\]

```{r}
# Group B: 
GroupB_test <- ca.jo(prices_KO_PEP, type = "trace", ecdet = "const", K = 2)
summary(GroupB_test)
```

The test results also indicate a cointegration relationship, these two assets tend to revert toward a long-run equilibrium. The identified cointegration relationship is:

\[
V - 0.2682 \times MA - 12.5970 = 0
\]

```{r}
# Group C:
GroupC_test <- ca.jo(prices_GLD_IAU, type = "trace", ecdet = "const", K = 2)
summary(GroupC_test)
```

The residual analysis plot for Group C (GLD & IAU) demonstrates that the cointegration relationship is stable over time, as the residuals fluctuate around the mean without significant divergence. This supports the long-term equilibrium relationship between the two gold ETFs.


\[
GLD - \beta \times IAU + \alpha = 0
\]



## 3.2 Spread Calculation and Trading Signals
To enhance adaptability to changing market conditions, we recommend employing a Kalman Filter-based time-varying cointegration estimation method instead of the conventional fixed-parameter approach. This allows for more accurate prediction of the spread and facilitates the generation of more stable and consistent returns

#Group A Visa and Mastercard:

The spread is calculated as:

\[
\text{spread} = V - 0.5453 \times MA - 23.6470
\]

A rolling mean and standard deviation with a 12-month window were computed to capture yearly market trends and minimize short-term volatility. The Z-score was calculated by:

\[
Z = \frac{\text{spread} - \text{rolling mean}}{\text{rolling standard deviation}}
\]

Trading signals based on Z-scores:

- **Long (1):** when \( Z < -1 \)

- **Short (-1):** when \( Z > 1 \)

- **No Position (0):** otherwise

```{r}
beta <- 0.5453
const_termA <- 23.6470

spreadA <- prices_V_MA[, "V"] - beta * prices_V_MA[, "MA"] - const_termA

spread_meanA <- rollapply(spreadA, width = 12, FUN = mean, align = "right", fill = NA)
spread_sdA <- rollapply(spreadA, width = 12, FUN = sd, align = "right", fill = NA)

z_scoreA <- (spreadA - spread_meanA) / spread_sdA

signalsA <- ifelse(z_scoreA < -1, 1, ifelse(z_scoreA > 1, -1, 0))
signalsA <- xts(signalsA, order.by = index(z_scoreA))

plot(z_scoreA, main = "Z-Score with Trading Signals", ylab = "Z-Score")
points(index(z_scoreA)[which(signalsA==1)], z_scoreA[signalsA==1], col = "green", pch = 16)
points(index(z_scoreA)[which(signalsA==-1)], z_scoreA[signalsA==-1], col = "red", pch = 16)
```

Trading signals were lagged by one period to simulate realistic trading conditions. Strategy returns were computed as follows:

\[
\text{strategy_return} = \frac{\text{lagged signal} \times \Delta \text{spread}}{\text{lagged spread}}
\]

Cumulative returns and key performance metrics, including the annualized Sharpe Ratio and Maximum Drawdown, were calculated:

```{r}
lag_signalsA <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(signalsA), n = 1), order.by = index(signalsA))
lag_spreadA <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(spreadA), n = 1), order.by = index(spreadA))
spread_diffA <- diff(spreadA)
strategy_returnsA <- na.omit(lag_signalsA * spread_diffA / lag_spreadA)

cumulative_returnsA <- cumprod(1 + strategy_returnsA) - 1
plot(cumulative_returnsA, main = "Cumulative Strategy Returns Group A", ylab = "Cumulative Returns Group A")

sharpe_A <- SharpeRatio.annualized(strategy_returnsA, Rf = 0)
mdd_A <- maxDrawdown(strategy_returnsA)

sharpe_A
mdd_A
```

### Group C: GLD and IAU Pair Trading Strategy

# Assume we already have GLD_adj, IAU_adj as xts from getSymbols

# Safest cointegration status check

    message("WARNING: GLD and IAU are not cointegrated. Proceed with caution.")

  }

alpha_C <- as.numeric(coef(egcm_test_C)["alpha"])

# 4. Demonstration of Kalman Filter Implementation

By utilizing the Kalman Filter to estimate time-varying cointegration coefficients, we enhance the accuracy of spread prediction in pair trading strategies.

```{r}
library(KFAS)

Y <- log(prices_V_MA)
model <- SSModel(Y[,1] ~ Y[,2], H = NA)
fit <- fitSSM(model, inits = c(0.1, 0.1), method = "BFGS")
kfs_result <- KFS(fit$model)

spread_kalman <- Y[,1] - coef(kfs_result)[,2] * Y[,2]

plot(spread_kalman, main = "Kalman Filter Estimated Spread for Visa & Mastercard", ylab = "Kalman Spread")
```

```{r}
# Group A: Visa & Mastercard
beta <- 0.5453
const_termA <- 23.6470
spreadA <- prices_V_MA[, "V"] - beta * prices_V_MA[, "MA"] - const_termA

spread_meanA <- rollapply(spreadA, width = 12, FUN = mean, align = "right", fill = NA)
spread_sdA <- rollapply(spreadA, width = 12, FUN = sd, align = "right", fill = NA)
z_scoreA <- (spreadA - spread_meanA) / spread_sdA

# Group B: Coca-Cola & Pepsi
beta <- 0.2682
const_termB <- 12.5970
spreadB <- prices_KO_PEP[, "KO"] - beta * prices_KO_PEP[, "PEP"] - const_termB

spread_meanB <- rollapply(spreadB, width = 12, FUN = mean, align = "right", fill = NA)
spread_sdB <- rollapply(spreadB, width = 12, FUN = sd, align = "right", fill = NA)
z_scoreB <- (spreadB - spread_meanB) / spread_sdB
```

```{r}
# Group C: GLD & IAU (based on Kalman Filter)
library(KFAS)

Y_C <- log(prices_GLD_IAU)
model_C <- SSModel(Y_C[,1] ~ Y_C[,2], H = NA)
fit_C <- fitSSM(model_C, inits = c(0.1, 0.1), method = "BFGS")
kfs_result_C <- KFS(fit_C$model)

spread_kalman_C <- Y_C[,1] - coef(kfs_result_C)[,2] * Y_C[,2]

plot(spread_kalman_C, main = "Kalman Filter Estimated Spread for GLD & IAU", ylab = "Kalman Spread")

beta_C <- mean(coef(kfs_result_C)[,2], na.rm = TRUE)
const_termC <- mean(coef(kfs_result_C)[,1], na.rm = TRUE)

spreadC <- prices_GLD_IAU[, "GLD"] - beta_C * prices_GLD_IAU[, "IAU"] - const_termC

spread_meanC <- rollapply(spreadC, width = 12, FUN = mean, align = "right", fill = NA)
spread_sdC <- rollapply(spreadC, width = 12, FUN = sd, align = "right", fill = NA)
z_scoreC <- (spreadC - spread_meanC) / spread_sdC

signalsC <- ifelse(z_scoreC < -1, 1, ifelse(z_scoreC > 1, -1, 0))
signalsC <- xts(signalsC, order.by = index(z_scoreC))

plot(z_scoreC, main = "Z-Score with Trading Signals (GLD & IAU)", ylab = "Z-Score")
points(index(z_scoreC)[which(signalsC==1)], z_scoreC[signalsC==1], col = "green", pch = 16)
points(index(z_scoreC)[which(signalsC==-1)], z_scoreC[signalsC==-1], col = "red", pch = 16)

lag_signalsC <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(signalsC), n = 1), order.by = index(signalsC))
lag_spreadC <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(spreadC), n = 1), order.by = index(spreadC))
spread_diffC <- diff(spreadC)
strategy_returnsC <- na.omit(lag_signalsC * spread_diffC / lag_spreadC)

cumulative_returnsC <- cumprod(1 + strategy_returnsC) - 1
plot(cumulative_returnsC, main = "Cumulative Strategy Returns Group C (GLD & IAU)", ylab = "Cumulative Returns")

sharpe_C <- SharpeRatio.annualized(strategy_returnsC, Rf = 0)
mdd_C <- maxDrawdown(strategy_returnsC)

sharpe_C
mdd_C


```





# 5. Performance Metrics Calculation
To evaluate the performance of the pair trading strategy, we compute the following five key performance metrics.
```{r}
# Group A
signalsA <- ifelse(z_scoreA < -1, 1, ifelse(z_scoreA > 1, -1, 0))
signalsA <- xts(signalsA, order.by = index(z_scoreA))

# Group B
signalsB <- ifelse(z_scoreB < -1, 1, ifelse(z_scoreB > 1, -1, 0))
signalsB <- xts(signalsB, order.by = index(z_scoreB))

# Group C
signalsC <- ifelse(z_scoreC < -1, 1, ifelse(z_scoreC > 1, -1, 0))
signalsC <- xts(signalsC, order.by = index(z_scoreC))

# Group A returns Calculation
lag_signalsA <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(signalsA), n = 1), order.by = index(signalsA))
lag_spreadA <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(spreadA), n = 1), order.by = index(spreadA))
spread_diffA <- diff(spreadA)
strategy_returnsA <- na.omit(lag_signalsA * spread_diffA / lag_spreadA)

# Group B returns Calculation
lag_signalsB <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(signalsB), n = 1), order.by = index(signalsB))
lag_spreadB <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(spreadB), n = 1), order.by = index(spreadB))
spread_diffB <- diff(spreadB)
strategy_returnsB <- na.omit(lag_signalsB * spread_diffB / lag_spreadB)

# Group C returns Calculation
lag_signalsC <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(signalsC), n = 1), order.by = index(signalsC))
lag_spreadC <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(spreadC), n = 1), order.by = index(spreadC))
spread_diffC <- diff(spreadC)
strategy_returnsC <- na.omit(lag_signalsC * spread_diffC / lag_spreadC)


# i) Cumulative P&L (Cumulative Profit and Loss)

cumPnL_A <- cumprod(1 + strategy_returnsA) - 1
cumPnL_B <- cumprod(1 + strategy_returnsB) - 1
cumPnL_C <- cumprod(1 + strategy_returnsC) - 1

plot(cumPnL_A, main = "Cumulative P&L for Visa & Mastercard", ylab = "Cumulative P&L")
plot(cumPnL_B, main = "Cumulative P&L for Coca-Cola & Pepsi", ylab = "Cumulative P&L")
plot(cumPnL_C, main = "Cumulative P&L for GLD & IAU", ylab = "Cumulative P&L Group C")


# ii) Sharpe Ratio Calculation
library(PerformanceAnalytics)

# Group A
strategy_returnsA_clean <- strategy_returnsA[is.finite(strategy_returnsA)]
sharpe_A <- SharpeRatio.annualized(strategy_returnsA_clean, Rf = 0, scale = 12)

# Group B
strategy_returnsB_clean <- strategy_returnsB[is.finite(strategy_returnsB)]
sharpe_B <- SharpeRatio.annualized(strategy_returnsB_clean, Rf = 0, scale = 12)

# Group C
strategy_returnsC_clean <- strategy_returnsC[is.finite(strategy_returnsC)]
sharpe_C <- SharpeRatio.annualized(strategy_returnsC_clean, Rf = 0, scale = 12)

# Print Results
sharpe_A
sharpe_B
sharpe_C


# iii) Maximum Drawdown
mdd_A <- maxDrawdown(strategy_returnsA)
mdd_B <- maxDrawdown(strategy_returnsB)
mdd_C <- maxDrawdown(strategy_returnsC)

mdd_A
mdd_B
mdd_C

chart.Drawdown(strategy_returnsA, main = "Drawdown: Visa & Mastercard")
chart.Drawdown(strategy_returnsB, main = "Drawdown: Coca-Cola & Pepsi")
chart.Drawdown(strategy_returnsC, main = "Drawdown: GLD & IAU")

# iv) Half-life
library(egcm)

half_life_A <- egcm(prices_V_MA$V, prices_V_MA$MA)$half.life
half_life_B <- egcm(prices_KO_PEP$KO, prices_KO_PEP$PEP)$half.life
half_life_C <- egcm(prices_GLD_IAU$GLD, prices_GLD_IAU$IAU)$half.life

half_life_A
half_life_B
half_life_C

# v) Winning Rate
win_rate_A <- sum(strategy_returnsA > 0) / length(strategy_returnsA[strategy_returnsA != 0])
win_rate_B <- sum(strategy_returnsB > 0) / length(strategy_returnsB[strategy_returnsB != 0])
win_rate_C <- sum(strategy_returnsC > 0) / length(strategy_returnsC[strategy_returnsC != 0])

win_rate_A
win_rate_B
win_rate_C



# Loop for comparing strategy performance across different Z-score thresholds
thresholds <- c(0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5)
results <- data.frame()

for (th in thresholds) {
  signals <- ifelse(z_scoreA < -th, 1, ifelse(z_scoreA > th, -1, 0))
  signals <- xts(signals, order.by = index(z_scoreA))

  lag_signals <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(signals), 1), order.by = index(signals))
  lag_spread <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(spreadA), 1), order.by = index(spreadA))
  spread_diff <- diff(spreadA)
  strategy_returns <- na.omit(lag_signals * spread_diff / lag_spread)

  sharpe <- SharpeRatio.annualized(strategy_returns, Rf = 0)
  mdd <- maxDrawdown(strategy_returns)
  win_rate <- sum(strategy_returns > 0) / length(strategy_returns[strategy_returns != 0])

  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(Zscore=th, Sharpe=sharpe, MDD=mdd, WinRate=win_rate))
}
print(results)

```

## 6. Time-Frame-Based Performance Comparison

To evaluate the robustness and stability of the pairs trading strategy under varying market conditions, the full sample period (2019–2024) was segmented into three distinct sub-periods. This temporal segmentation enables a more granular assessment of the strategy's performance across different economic environments and facilitates the identification of potential sensitivity to major external shocks, such as the COVID-19 pandemic and interest rate hikes. By re-estimating performance within each sub-period, we aim to determine whether the strategy demonstrates consistent efficacy or exhibits significant variation in response to macroeconomic events.

```{r}
# Define the sub-periods correctly:
periods <- list(
  list(start = as.Date("2019-01-01"), end = as.Date("2020-12-31")),
  list(start = as.Date("2021-01-01"), end = as.Date("2022-12-31")),
  list(start = as.Date("2023-01-01"), end = as.Date("2024-01-01"))
)

# Analysis Function per Group
analyze_group <- function(prices, beta, const_term){
  results <- data.frame()

for (p in periods) {
    prices_period <- window(prices, start = p$start, end = p$end)

    spread <- prices_period[,1] - beta * prices_period[,2] - const_term
    spread_mean <- rollapply(spread, width=12, FUN=mean, align="right", fill=NA)
    spread_sd <- rollapply(spread, width=12, FUN=sd, align="right", fill=NA)
    z_score <- (spread - spread_mean) / spread_sd

    signals <- ifelse(z_score < -1, 1, ifelse(z_score > 1, -1, 0))
    signals <- xts(signals, order.by=index(z_score))

    lag_signals <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(signals),1), order.by=index(signals))
    lag_spread <- xts(dplyr::lag(coredata(spread),1), order.by=index(spread))
    spread_diff <- diff(spread)
    strategy_returns <- na.omit(lag_signals * spread_diff / lag_spread)

    metrics <- calculate_metrics(strategy_returns)

    results <- rbind(results, metrics)
}


  colnames(results) <- c("Cumulative_PnL", "Sharpe_Ratio", "Max_Drawdown", "Win_Rate")
  rownames(results) <- c("2019-2020", "2021-2022", "2023-2024")
  return(results)
}
```

# Group A (Visa & Mastercard)
results_A <- analyze_group(prices_V_MA, beta = 0.5453, const_term = 23.6470)
cat("\n### Performance Summary by Time Frame (Visa & Mastercard)\n")
print(results_A)

# Group B (Coca-Cola & Pepsi)
results_B <- analyze_group(prices_KO_PEP, beta = 0.2682, const_term = 12.5970)
cat("\n### Performance Summary by Time Frame (Coca-Cola & Pepsi)\n")
print(results_B)

# Group C (GLD & IAU)
results_C <- analyze_group(prices_GLD_IAU, beta = beta_C, const_term = const_termC)
cat("\n### Performance Summary by Time Frame (GLD & IAU)\n")
print(results_C)
